name: Open Collective

sources.title: Homepage — collaborative money management; splits sign-up by legally incorporated vs unincorporated projects
For Collectives — 'Create a Collective' links to /signup/collective; explains fiscal hosting requirement
Batch-provided submission URL — rendered only a nav shell, no form

conditions: Creating a collective is free, but to receive money the collective must be accepted by a fiscal host (e.g. Open Source Collective, Open Collective Europe, Gift Collective) — each host has its own mission scope, geography, acceptance criteria and fees
This is a fundraising/fiscal-hosting platform, not a launch directory — only appropriate for products/projects that genuinely want to accept donations or sponsorships transparently
requirements: Project fits a fiscal host's mission scope (e.g. open source projects → Open Source Collective 501(c)(6); European groups → Open Collective Europe; charitable NZ groups → Gift Collective)
Collective pages are financially transparent by design — balances, contributions and expenses are public
Commercial SaaS looking for a backlink/launch listing is not the intended use
preparation: Decide which fiscal host matches the project's mission, location and currency
Project name, description, public repo/community links
Admin real-name identity — finances are publicly attributed
Planned contribution tiers (tip jar, monthly goals, memberships) if fundraising is the goal
workflow: Create the collective profile (name, mission, links)
Apply to a suitable fiscal host from the collective dashboard — hosts review against their acceptance criteria
After host approval, the public collective page at opencollective.com/<slug> is live and can accept contributions
watchFor: Batch submission URL /create renders an empty nav shell — the real route is /signup/collective
Fiscal host review is a gate: rejection leaves the page without money features
All finances are public — do not use for a product that shouldn't disclose revenue
Host fees differ per host (typically a % of funds raised) — 'free' refers to page creation
countsAsLive: The collective page is publicly reachable at opencollective.com/<slug> and, once host-approved, shows an active 'Contribute' option
unknowns: Exact acceptance criteria and turnaround per fiscal host
Whether a purely commercial SaaS product would be accepted by any host
